title_original: Chris Rock, Quinta Brunson, Jaafar Jackson, Chiwetel Ejiofor Among Honorees For 9th Critics Choice Celebration Of Black Cinema & TV
excerpt_original: It is a star-studded lineup for the Critics Choice Association’s ninth annual Celebration of Black Cinema & Television. Debbie Allen, Chris Rock, Quinta Brunson, Jaafar Jackson and Chiwetel Ejiofor are among this year’s honorees for this year’s event, taking place November 16…

blocks.text: It is a star-studded lineup for the Critics Choice Association’s ninth annual Celebration of Black Cinema & Television.

Debbie Allen , Chris Rock , Quinta Brunson , Jaafar Jackson and Chiwetel Ejiofor are among this year’s honorees for this year’s event, taking place November 16 and highlighting standout performances and work, both onscreen and offscreen, from the Black entertainment community. Roy Wood Jr. hosts the show.

blocks.text: “We are proud to announce that the celebration continues,” said Shawn Edwards, executive producer and writer of the Critics Choice Association’s Celebration of Black Cinema & Television. “At a time when there has been a direct assault on Black culture and Black history, the Critics Choice Association stands firmly committed to recognizing the best in Black cinema and television. This isn’t something that we have to do, it’s something that we want to do. Creating a space where these bold and visionary storytellers can come together for an evening and be honored is our privilege and something that we are firmly committed to doing each year.”
Honorees for this year’s Celebration of Black Cinema & Television will include, per the CCA:
Watch on Deadline

Academy Honorary Award recipient, six-time Emmy winner, and two-time Tony nominee Debbie Allen will receive the Icon Award, recognizing her extraordinary career and enduring cultural impact across nearly five decades, with more than 140 acting, producing, and directing credits. Her tribute will celebrate the legacy of A Different World and its 2026 Netflix sequel, bringing the Black college experience to a new generation. Allen produced the original series and directed 83 of its 144 episodes, helping shape a groundbreaking show that addressed HIV, colorism, and racism. She returns as executive producer and director of the sequel and reprises her role as Dr. Langhorne. The series has already been renewed for a second season.

Two-time Emmy Award winner and Critics Choice Award winner Quinta Brunson will receive the Groundbreaker Award for creating, executive producing, and starring in ABC’s Abbott Elementary , which premiered its sixth season on Oct. 7. Produced by Warner Bros. Television & 20th Television, the hit comedy has earned 37 Emmy nominations to date. Brunson made Emmy history in 2022 as the first solo Black woman to win for comedy writing, and in 2024 she became the first Black actress in more than 40 years to win Outstanding Lead Actress in a Comedy Series.

Academy Award and Critics Choice Award nominee Chiwetel Ejiofor will receive the Vanguard Award for his work in A24’s psychological horror film Backrooms . Directed by Kane Parsons, the horror hit opened to $81.4 million domestically, shattering the previous record for an A24 opening weekend release and becoming its highest-grossing film to date, earning more than $400 million worldwide. Ejiofor leads the cast alongside Renate Reinsve in the adaptation of Parsons’ viral YouTube series.

Emmy and Grammy Award winner Chris Rock will receive the Director Award for A24’s Misty Green . The film marks Rock’s fourth narrative feature as a director. He also wrote, produced, and co-stars in the film, which stars Rosalind Eleazar ( Slow Horses) in a career-defining turn portraying an actress fighting to revive her career.

Emmy Award winner Lamorne Morris will receive the Comedy Award for his work as Robbie Robertson in Prime Video’s superhero series Spider-Noir. The series earned 11 Emmy nominations, and won five Emmy Awards.

Pulitzer Prize winner Katori Hall will be honored with the Showrunner Award for Starz’s P-Valley . The series returns December 4 for its third and final season with a two-episode premiere. Hall created the series from her own play and directed both premiere episodes. P-Valley is Starz’s best-performing current original, with Season 2 averaging 11.6 million multiplatform viewers.

Jaafar Jackson will receive the Actor Award – Film for his critically acclaimed, crowd-pleasing portrayal of Michael Jackson in Lionsgate’s biographical film Michael , which marks his acting debut. The film set records not only for a music biopic—it became the first biopic of any kind to gross more than $1 billion worldwide and is the most successful release in Lionsgate history.

Emmy Award nominee Anthony Mackie will be honored with the Actor Award – Series for his work in Apple TV’s upcoming 12 12 12 , which he also executive produces. Mackie plays a disgraced FBI agent locked in a cat-and-mouse game across Europe with Jamie Dornan’s career criminal, in the eight-episode heist drama. 12 12 12 premieres globally on Apple TV on Nov. 13.

Emmy nominee Stephan James will be honored with the Supporting Actor Award – Film for his portrayal of Carl Weathers in Amazon MGM Studios’ I Play Rocky . Directed by Academy Award winner Peter Farrelly, the film chronicles the making of the original Rocky and Sylvester Stallone’s determination to write and star in it. The biographical drama opens in November.

Tony Award winner and Academy Award and Emmy nominee Sophie Okonedo will receive the Supporting Actress Award – Film for her performance in Independent Film Company’s coming-of-age drama Mouse , directed by Kelly O’Sullivan and Alex Thompson. The drama premiered at the Berlin Film Festival and begins its theatrical engagements next month.

SAG Award and Critics Choice Award nominee Ato Essandoh will receive the Supporting Actor Award – Series for his work as Stuart Hayford in Netflix’s drama series The Diplomat. The political thriller was nominated for Outstanding Drama Series at the Emmys in 2025 and again in 2026, and returned for its fourth season October 15.

Tony Award nominee Quincy Tyler Bernstine will receive the Supporting Actress Award – Series for her work as Nora Washington in Hulu’s Furious . Created by Elizabeth Meriwether, the thriller follows an FBI agent hunting a calculating female serial killer. Bernstine’s attention-grabbing performance has emerged as a standout in one of the most buzzed-about new series of 2026.

Additionally, Starz will bestow on Bernstine’s award a special Starz #TakeTheLead designation as part of its ongoing commitment to amplifying narratives by, about, and for women and underrepresented audiences.

Emerging filmmakers Arie Esiri and Chuko Esiri will receive the Breakthrough Director Award for Neon’s Clarissa , a reimagining of Virginia Woolf’s Mrs. Dalloway set in contemporary Lagos, Nigeria. The film stars fellow Celebration of Black Cinema & Television honoree Okonedo alongside David Oyelowo, Ayo Edebiri, India Amarteifio and Toheeb Jimoh. It premiered in the Directors’ Fortnight section of the 2026 Cannes Film Festival, becoming only the second Nigerian feature ever selected by the festival and opens in select theaters December 11.

Jaalen Best will be honored with the Rising Star Award for his performance as Cassius Clay in Prime Video’s Muhammad Ali biographical drama series, The Greatest . It is the first authorized scripted series about Ali’s life, with executive producers including his widow Lonnie Ali, as well as Josh Wakely and Michael B. Jordan. The series premieres on Prime Video on November 4.
The Critics Choice Association’s Celebration of Black Cinema & Television will be produced by Madelyn Hammond, Javier Infante and Ella Carlson of Hammond Infante Productions.
